## Q1
If in Delhi, the number of employees who work in Accounts is 40% more than the number who work in HR, what is the number of employees who work in IT in Delhi?

The following table shows the number of employees in an organization in five cities. The total number of employees is 4,260. Percentages show distribution across HR, Finance, IT and Accounts. Some values are missing and may be calculated when required. Each employee works in only one department.

| City | Employees | HR | Finance | IT | Accounts |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Delhi | 900 | - | 18% | - | 28% |
| Mumbai | 760 | 15% | - | 30% | - |
| Bengaluru | - | 18% | 20% | - | 32% |
| Hyderabad | - | - | 25% | 18% | 35% |
| Gurgaon | 700 | 20% | 22% | - | 20% |

## Q1 - Options
(A) 266
(B) 306
(C) 352
(D) 294

## Q1 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Data Interpretation
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q1

In Delhi, total employees = 900. Accounts = 28% of 900 = 252.<br>
The number of Accounts employees is 40% more than HR employees. Let HR employees be x.<br>
x + 0.4x = 252 -&gt; 1.4x = 252 -&gt; x = 180.<br>
HR percentage = (180 / 900) \* 100 = 20%.<br>
Total percentage of HR, Finance, and Accounts = 20% + 18% + 28% = 66%.<br>
Therefore, IT percentage = 100% - 66% = 34%.<br>
Number of IT employees in Delhi = 34% of 900 = 306.

## Q2
What is the total number of employees in Mumbai and Gurgaon who work in the IT department?

The following table shows the number of employees in an organization in five cities. The total number of employees is 4,260. Percentages show distribution across HR, Finance, IT and Accounts. Some values are missing and may be calculated when required. Each employee works in only one department.

| City | Employees | HR | Finance | IT | Accounts |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Delhi | 900 | - | 18% | - | 28% |
| Mumbai | 760 | 15% | - | 30% | - |
| Bengaluru | - | 18% | 20% | - | 32% |
| Hyderabad | - | - | 25% | 18% | 35% |
| Gurgaon | 700 | 20% | 22% | - | 20% |

## Q2 - Options
(A) 482
(B) 452
(C) 570
(D) 494

## Q2 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Data Interpretation
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q2

In Mumbai, total employees = 760. IT percentage = 30%. Number of IT employees = 30% of 760 = 228.<br>
In Gurgaon, total employees = 700. The sum of other departments' percentages is HR(20%) + Finance(22%) + Accounts(20%) = 62%.<br>
IT percentage in Gurgaon = 100% - 62% = 38%.<br>
Number of IT employees in Gurgaon = 38% of 700 = 266.<br>
Total IT employees in Mumbai and Gurgaon = 228 + 266 = 494.

## Q3
If the number of employees in Bengaluru is 10% less than the number in Hyderabad, what is the difference between the total number of employees working in the Accounts department and the total number working in the Finance department across these two cities?

The following table shows the number of employees in an organization in five cities. The total number of employees is 4,260. Percentages show distribution across HR, Finance, IT and Accounts. Some values are missing and may be calculated when required. Each employee works in only one department.

| City | Employees | HR | Finance | IT | Accounts |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Delhi | 900 | - | 18% | - | 28% |
| Mumbai | 760 | 15% | - | 30% | - |
| Bengaluru | - | 18% | 20% | - | 32% |
| Hyderabad | - | - | 25% | 18% | 35% |
| Gurgaon | 700 | 20% | 22% | - | 20% |

## Q3 - Options
(A) 244
(B) 208
(C) 194
(D) 270

## Q3 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Data Interpretation
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q3

The total number of employees across all five cities is 4260.<br>
Employees in Delhi + Mumbai + Gurgaon = 900 + 760 + 700 = 2360.<br>
Employees in Bengaluru + Hyderabad = 4260 - 2360 = 1900.<br>
Let the number of employees in Hyderabad be H. The number in Bengaluru is 0.9H.<br>
0.9H + H = 1900 -&gt; 1.9H = 1900 -&gt; H = 1000. So, Bengaluru has 900 employees.<br>
In Bengaluru: Finance = 20% of 900 = 180; Accounts = 32% of 900 = 288.<br>
In Hyderabad: Finance = 25% of 1000 = 250; Accounts = 35% of 1000 = 350.<br>
Total Finance = 180 + 250 = 430.<br>
Total Accounts = 288 + 350 = 638.<br>
Difference = 638 - 430 = 208.

## Q5

The following table shows the number of employees in an organization in five cities. The total number of employees is 4,260. Percentages show distribution across HR, Finance, IT and Accounts. Some values are missing and may be calculated when required. Each employee works in only one department.

| City | Employees | HR | Finance | IT | Accounts |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Delhi | 900 | - | 18% | - | 28% |
| Mumbai | 760 | 15% | - | 30% | - |
| Bengaluru | - | 18% | 20% | - | 32% |
| Hyderabad | - | - | 25% | 18% | 35% |
| Gurgaon | 700 | 20% | 22% | - | 20% |

## Q5 - Options
(A) Two
(B) Three
(C) Four
(D) Five

## Q5 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Data Interpretation
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q5

Using the data from question 3, Bengaluru = 900 and Hyderabad = 1000 employees.<br>
Let's calculate Finance + Accounts for each city:<br>
Delhi: (18% + 28%) = 46% of 900 = 414.<br>
Mumbai: We know HR (15%) + IT (30%) = 45%, so Finance + Accounts must be 55%. 55% of 760 = 418.<br>
Bengaluru: Finance (20%) + Accounts (32%) = 52% of 900 = 468.<br>
Hyderabad: Finance (25%) + Accounts (35%) = 60% of 1000 = 600.<br>
Gurgaon: Finance (22%) + Accounts (20%) = 42% of 700 = 294.<br>
The total exceeds 415 in exactly three cities: Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad.

## Q6
When you sign up for something like a free e-mail account, you may be presented with a CAPTCHA. CAPTCHA stands for:

## Q6 - Options
(A) Coverage Analysis and Planning Tool for Computers and Humans Apart
(B) Completely Automated Public Turing Test to Tell Computers and Humans Apart
(C) Completely Applied Parallel Technologies for Communication and Hardware Apart
(D) Comparable Additional Protected Turing Test to Tell Computers and Humans Apart

## Q6 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** ICT (Computers, Internet, Terminology)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q6

CAPTCHA stands for 'Completely Automated Public Turing test to tell Computers and Humans Apart'. It is named after the Turing Test, proposed by Alan Turing in 1950, which tests whether a machine can exhibit behaviour indistinguishable from a human. A CAPTCHA reverses this concept — it is a test *designed by a computer* to determine whether the respondent is a human or an automated bot. Common forms include distorted text, image recognition challenges, and checkbox challenges. It is widely used to prevent spam, automated account creation, and brute-force attacks.

## Q8
Which of the following arguments commits the fallacy of contradicted middle such that the middle term, instead of being pervaded by the presence of the major term, is pervaded by the absence of the major term?

## Q8 - Options
(A) All things are non-eternal because they are knowable.
(B) Sound is a quality because it is visible.
(C) Fire is cold because it is a substance.
(D) Sound is eternal because it is produced.

## Q8 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Logical Reasoning: Indian Logic
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q8

The fallacy of a contradicted middle (Viruddha) occurs when the middle term establishes the exact opposite of the major term. In 'Sound is eternal because it is produced', being 'produced' is a characteristic of non-eternal things, directly contradicting the claim that sound is eternal.

## Q9
A photovoltaic array is:

## Q9 - Options
(A) A single solar cell
(B) A single solar module
(C) A single solar panel
(D) A combination of solar panels

## Q9 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Environment (Pollution, Climate, Resources, Hazards)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q9

Solar energy generation is organised in a clear hierarchy:

- **Solar cell:** The smallest unit; a single semiconductor device (typically silicon) that converts sunlight into electricity via the photovoltaic effect.
- **Solar module / panel:** Multiple solar cells electrically wired together and encapsulated in a protective frame.
- **Photovoltaic array:** Multiple solar panels (modules) connected together — in series, parallel, or a combination — to form a complete power-generating installation. Arrays can range from a rooftop setup to a utility-scale solar farm. An array is therefore never a single cell, module, or panel.

## Q11
Given below are two statements:<br>
Statement I: The risk of rejecting the null hypothesis when it should be confirmed is more at the 0.05 p-level than at the 0.01 p-level.<br>
Statement II: The risk of committing a Type-I error is lower at the 0.05 p-level than at the 0.01 p-level.

## Q11 - Options
(A) Both Statement I and Statement II are true
(B) Both Statement I and Statement II are false
(C) Statement I is true but Statement II is false
(D) Statement I is false but Statement II is true

## Q11 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Research Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q11

A Type I error is rejecting the null hypothesis when it is actually true (a 'false positive'). The probability of committing a Type I error equals the significance level (α).

- At α = 0.05, there is a 5% chance of a Type I error.
- At α = 0.01, there is only a 1% chance of a Type I error.

Therefore, the risk of a Type I error is **higher** at 0.05 than at 0.01, making Statement I true. Statement II says the risk is **lower** at 0.05, which directly contradicts the definition — so Statement II is false. A stricter (smaller) significance level reduces the probability of rejecting a true null hypothesis.

## Q12
Given below are two statements:<br>
Statement I: There is an argument that the emergence of cable and television audiences has brought in a more personalised and interactive media culture.<br>
Statement II: Within an integrated communication system, messages do not acquire communicability and socialisation.

## Q12 - Options
(A) Both Statement I and Statement II are true
(B) Both Statement I and Statement II are false
(C) Statement I is true but Statement II is false
(D) Statement I is false but Statement II is true

## Q12 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Communication
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q12

Statement I is correct. The rise of cable television, satellite channels, and later internet-based streaming fragmented the mass broadcast audience into numerous niche audiences, enabling more personalised, on-demand, and interactive media consumption — a shift scholars call the 'second media age' or the era of narrowcasting.

Statement II is false. An integrated communication system is specifically designed to maximise communicability — the capacity of messages to be understood — and to facilitate socialisation by coordinating multiple channels (text, audio, video, social media) into a unified framework. Messages in such a system acquire *greater* communicability, not less.

## Q14
Media interactivity is experienced at different levels in different \_\_\_\_\_\_ relations.

## Q14 - Options
(A) Political
(B) Economic
(C) Techno-social
(D) Techno-ethical

## Q14 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Communication
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q14

Media interactivity refers to the degree to which users can influence the form and content of a mediated environment. This interactivity does not operate uniformly; it is shaped by the intersection of technological infrastructure and the social norms, habits, and relationships of users — collectively called techno-social relations. Different techno-social contexts (e.g., a rural community with limited broadband vs. an urban professional network) experience and exercise media interactivity differently. The concept bridges purely technical affordances with the social practices that determine how those affordances are actually used.

## Q17
Determine the next term in the number series: 3, 15, 35, 63, ?

## Q17 - Options
(A) 89
(B) 91
(C) 99
(D) 106

## Q17 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Mathematical Reasoning (Series, Coding, Relationships)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q17

The pattern is formed by the squares of consecutive even numbers minus 1:<br>
2^2 - 1 = 3<br>
4^2 - 1 = 15<br>
6^2 - 1 = 35<br>
8^2 - 1 = 63<br>
Following this pattern, the next term is 10^2 - 1 = 99.

## Q19
Given below are two statements:<br>
Statement I: A dichotomous variable is one which has more than two categories.<br>
Statement II: A nominal variable can have more than two categories.

## Q19 - Options
(A) Both Statement I and Statement II are true
(B) Both Statement I and Statement II are false
(C) Statement I is true but Statement II is false
(D) Statement I is false but Statement II is true

## Q19 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Research Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q19

A **dichotomous variable** has exactly two mutually exclusive categories — for example, Yes/No, Employed/Unemployed, or Heads/Tails. It cannot have more than two categories, making Statement I false.

A **nominal variable** classifies observations into named categories without any intrinsic order or ranking. It can have two categories (making it dichotomous) or many more — for example, type of religion (Hindu, Muslim, Christian, Buddhist, …), blood group (A, B, AB, O), or country of birth. Statement II is therefore true.

## Q21
The Union Government's mandate for the Humayun Kabir Committee was to explore the possibility of:

## Q21 - Options
(A) Privatisation of public universities
(B) Setting up of new university
(C) Establishing correspondence courses
(D) Funding private universities

**Answer:** B

**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q21

The Humayun Kabir Committee (1964) was appointed by the Union Government to review the growing pressure on India's higher education system. ## Q22
A passenger train running at 75 km/hr leaves a railway station 9 hours after a goods train leaves and overtakes it in 6 hours. The speed of the goods train is:

## Q22 - Options
(A) 35 km/hr
(B) 32 km/hr
(C) 30 km/hr
(D) 28 km/hr

## Q22 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Mathematical Aptitude (Arithmetic)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q22

The passenger train travels for 6 hours before overtaking. Distance covered = 75 km/hr \* 6 hr = 450 km.<br>
The goods train has been traveling for 9 + 6 = 15 hours to reach the same distance.<br>
Speed of goods train = Distance / Time = 450 km / 15 hr = 30 km/hr.

## Q23
In a certain coding scheme, 'WOMEN' is coded as '70'. How will 'CHILDREN' be coded in this scheme?

## Q23 - Options
(A) 178
(B) 143
(C) 116
(D) 73

## Q23 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Mathematical Reasoning (Series, Coding, Relationships)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q23

In this coding scheme, 'WOMEN' is coded as '70'. Summing the alphabetical positions of WOMEN (W=23, O=15, M=13, E=5, N=14): 23 + 15 + 13 + 5 + 14 = 70. Applying the same logic to 'CHILDREN': C=3, H=8, I=9, L=12, D=4, R=18, E=5, N=14. The sum is 3 + 8 + 9 + 12 + 4 + 18 + 5 + 14 = 73. Therefore, the correct code is 73.

## Q24
According to UGC Regulations 2018 on plagiarism, common knowledge or coincidental terms up to how many consecutive words shall be excluded while checking similarity for detection of plagiarism?

## Q24 - Options
(A) 8
(B) 12
(C) 14
(D) 18

## Q24 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Research Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q24

The UGC (Promotion of Academic Integrity and Prevention of Plagiarism in Higher Educational Institutions) Regulations, 2018 specify that the following shall be **excluded** from similarity detection:

- Properly attributed quotations
- References and bibliography
- Standard symbols, equations, and formulae
- Table of contents, preface, and acknowledgements
- **Common knowledge or coincidental terms up to 14 consecutive words**

The 14-word threshold prevents routine phrases and widely-shared knowledge from inflating similarity scores. This exclusion applies per matched segment — any run of identical text shorter than 14 words is not flagged as plagiarism.

## Q25
If x = 0.25 and y = 0.16, find the value of the expression: y/x + √x × √y - xy

## Q25 - Options
(A) 0.6
(B) 0.8
(C) 0.45
(D) 0.58

## Q25 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Mathematical Aptitude (Arithmetic)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q25

Given x = 0.25 and y = 0.16.<br>
First term: y/x = 0.16 / 0.25 = 16/25 = 0.64.<br>
Second term: √x = 0.5 and √y = 0.4. Therefore, √x \* √y = 0.5 \* 0.4 = 0.20.<br>
Third term: xy = 0.25 \* 0.16 = 0.04.<br>
Total expression = 0.64 + 0.20 - 0.04 = 0.84 - 0.04 = 0.8.

## Q27

(A) =IF(C3&gt;=B3,IF(C4&gt;B4,"Yes","No"),"No")

**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q27

Since both the Midterm and Final exam conditions must be satisfied simultaneously, a logical AND is required — the student is allowed only if *both* results meet the minimums.

**Option B** — `=IF(AND(C3>=B3,C4>=B4),"Yes","No")` — correctly checks both conditions with `>=` (greater than or equal to) for each.

**Why other options fail:**

- **Option A** uses `C4>B4` (strict greater-than) for the final exam. If the student scores exactly the minimum (e.g., 75 vs 75 needed), Option A would return 'No' even though the condition is met — a subtle but critical bug.
- **Option C** uses an array range (`C3:C4>=B3:B4`) which does not work as a single TRUE/FALSE in a standard IF formula.
- **Option D** uses OR, meaning the student passes if *either* condition is met — but both must be met per the stated rule.

## Q28
The process of comparing a student's performance against his/her previous performance is known as:

## Q28 - Options
(A) Diagnostic evaluation
(B) Summative assessment
(C) Ipsative assessment
(D) Informal assessment

## Q28 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Teaching Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q28

Assessment can be measured against three reference points:

- **Norm-referenced:** A student's performance is compared to the group average (e.g., class rank).
- **Criterion-referenced / Summative:** Performance is measured against a fixed external standard (e.g., scoring ≥ 50% to pass).
- **Ipsative assessment:** Performance is compared to the student's *own previous performance*. The term comes from the Latin 'ipse' meaning 'self'. It focuses on personal growth and improvement over time, regardless of external benchmarks or peer comparison.

Ipsative assessment is widely used in sport, rehabilitation, and personalised learning contexts where individual progress matters more than peer ranking.

## Q31
When people metacommunicate, they are sending messages about:

## Q31 - Options
(A) Senders
(B) Receivers
(C) Channels
(D) Messages

## Q31 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Communication
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q31

Communication theorist Gregory Bateson introduced the concept of metacommunication — communication *about* communication itself. When people metacommunicate, they are sending messages that frame, qualify, or comment on other messages in the interaction.

For example, saying "I was only joking" after a statement is metacommunication — it is a message *about* the preceding message. Tone of voice, facial expression, and framing devices like "to be serious for a moment…" are all forms of metacommunication. It operates at a higher logical level than the message content itself, shaping how the receiver should interpret the message.

## Q32
Given below are two statements:<br>
Statement I: The electronic space of the Internet has failed to displace institutional space in a society even an iota.<br>
Statement II: Internet communication has broken down the hierarchies of race, ethnicity and gender.

## Q32 - Options
(A) Both Statement I and Statement II are true
(B) Both Statement I and Statement II are false
(C) Statement I is true but Statement II is false
(D) Statement I is false but Statement II is true

## Q32 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Communication
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q32

Statement I is false. The Internet has significantly displaced and disrupted traditional institutional spaces — journalism, retail, education, banking, and government services have all been profoundly restructured by digital and online platforms. Claiming the Internet has not displaced institutional space 'even an iota' is empirically indefensible.

Statement II is considered true within the context of media and communication theory: the Internet has created democratised spaces where individuals can publish, organise, and interact regardless of race, ethnicity, or gender in ways that traditional hierarchical institutional spaces did not permit. While discrimination persists online, the structural barriers to voice and participation are considerably lower than in pre-internet institutional contexts.

## Q37
What is the correct increasing order of contribution to global warming by the following gases?<br>
A. Methane (CH4)<br>
B. Carbon dioxide (CO2)<br>
C. Nitrous oxide (N2O)

## Q37 - Options
(A) A, B, C
(B) C, A, B
(C) B, A, C
(D) B, C, A

## Q37 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Environment (Pollution, Climate, Resources, Hazards)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q37

When measuring **total contribution to global warming**, what matters is the total radiative forcing each gas exerts on the atmosphere — which depends on both its warming potency per molecule *and* its actual atmospheric concentration.

- **CO₂:** Low warming potential per molecule (GWP = 1) but present in massive quantities; responsible for roughly 66–76% of total anthropogenic warming.
- **CH₄ (Methane):** Much higher GWP per molecule (~28–84×) but far less abundant; contributes roughly 16–18%.
- **N₂O (Nitrous oxide):** Very high GWP per molecule (~265–298×) but extremely low concentration; contributes roughly 6%.

Increasing order of total contribution: N₂O (C) &lt; CH₄ (A) &lt; CO₂ (B) → answer option B (C, A, B).

## Q38
If A, B and C can complete a piece of work in 3, 5 and 6 days respectively, they together will complete the work in:

## Q38 - Options
(A) 1 3/7 days
(B) 2 4/7 days
(C) 1 1/2 days
(D) 2 1/3 days

## Q38 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** Mathematical Aptitude (Arithmetic)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q38

A's 1-day work = 1/3, B's = 1/5, C's = 1/6. Total 1-day work = 1/3 + 1/5 + 1/6 = (10+6+5)/30 = 21/30 = 7/10. Therefore, together they will finish the work in 10/7 days, which is 1 3/7 days.

## Q42
As per the recommendation of the National Education Policy (2020), Indian standards of skills will be aligned with the International Standard Classification of Occupations of:

## Q42 - Options
(A) UNDP
(B) UNESCO
(C) ILO
(D) ITU

## Q42 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Higher Education System
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q42

The National Education Policy 2020 (NEP 2020) sets out to map Indian skill qualifications onto a globally recognisable framework. It specifies alignment with the **International Standard Classification of Occupations (ISCO)**, which is maintained by the **International Labour Organization (ILO)** — the UN agency responsible for labour standards.

ISCO provides a hierarchical system for classifying and organising all occupations, enabling comparison of skill levels and job families across countries. This alignment allows Indian vocational and higher-education qualifications to be benchmarked and recognised internationally. The other options (UNDP — development finance; UNESCO — education/culture; ITU — telecommunications) do not maintain occupational classification standards.

## Q43

C. Feline<br>
D. Animal

(A) A, C, B, D
(B) D, A, C, B
(C) D, B, C, A
(D) A, B, C, D

## Q43 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Logical Reasoning (Venn, Syllogism, Arguments)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q43

Intension refers to the specific qualities or attributes a term possesses. As intension increases, the term becomes more specific. The increasing order of specificity (intension) is Animal -&gt; Mammal -&gt; Feline -&gt; Tiger. Hence, D, B, C, A.

## Q44
Identify the formal fallacy committed in the following argument: "Some good actors are not powerful athletes. All professional wrestlers are powerful athletes. Therefore all professional wrestlers are good actors."

## Q44 - Options
(A) Exclusive premises
(B) Existential fallacy
(C) Affirmative conclusion from negative premises
(D) Affirming the consequent

## Q44 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Logical Reasoning (Venn, Syllogism, Arguments)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q44

The premise "Some good actors are not powerful athletes" is negative. A fundamental rule of syllogism states that if a premise is negative, the conclusion must also be negative. Drawing an affirmative conclusion violates this rule, causing the fallacy of drawing an affirmative conclusion from a negative premise.

## Q45
United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) was the outcome of:

## Q45 - Options
(A) Paris Agreement
(B) Montreal Protocol
(C) Convention on Biodiversity
(D) Earth Summit

## Q45 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** People, Development & Environmental Policy
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q45

The **United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)** was one of the landmark agreements produced at the **Earth Summit** — formally the United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (UNCED) — held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, in June 1992. The Earth Summit also produced the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) and Agenda 21.

The UNFCCC entered into force in 1994 and provides the legal framework under which subsequent climate agreements operate, including the Kyoto Protocol (1997) and the Paris Agreement (2015).

The other options are incorrect because:

- The **Paris Agreement (A)** is itself a *product* of the UNFCCC process, not the other way around.
- The **Montreal Protocol (B)** addresses ozone-depleting substances, not greenhouse gas emissions.
- The **Convention on Biodiversity (C)** was signed at the same Earth Summit but is a separate treaty.
